name: lm-format-enforcer
notable_features: Mechanism: a character-level incremental parser feeds a prefix-allowed-tokens function, so the model is only ever offered tokens that keep the output parseable. Different in kind from grammar-automaton approaches
Supports JSON Schema, schemaless JSON mode and regular expressions; required and optional fields, nested fields, arrays and dictionaries
Explicitly lets the LLM control whitespace and field ordering in JSON rather than forcing canonical output, which the README argues reduces hallucination of structural noise
Supports batched generation and beam search with a different token filter per input or per beam - the README's comparison table marks this as a capability guidance and jsonformer lack
Was integrated into the vLLM OpenAI server as `--guided-decoding-backend lm-format-enforcer`, documented in the README with a full request example
Does not modify the transformers high-level loop, so it drops into existing pipelines
Small and honest: the README includes a capability comparison table against guidance, jsonformer and outlines in which it loses several rows
MIT, 2042 stars, last release v0.11.2 (2025-08-09), last push 2026-04-04
hardware_caveats: Superseded as a default, and its own README's comparison table concedes ground. It is no longer vLLM's default structured-generation backend - XGrammar took that role (see [[niche-xgrammar]]). Current state: a small library that still works and still has a documented vLLM integration path

The guidance row in its comparison table marks Guidance as lacking batched generation and beam search, and Outlines as lacking optional JSON fields and LLM-controlled ordering. Treat the table as the maintainer's own view, not neutral
Pure Python per-token work: a character-level parser run at every decode step is more Python overhead than a C++ automaton, which is the practical reason for the demotion
Requires a logits-level hook in the host process, so it works in-process with transformers and (historically) vLLM, but not against a remote HTTP endpoint
Release cadence has slowed: v0.11.2 from 2025-08-09 while the last push was 2026-04-04. Actively receiving commits, not actively cutting versions

Legacy Python library: the README's own install line pulls transformers, torch, huggingface_hub and optimum, so it inherits the heavy dependency set that motivated xgrammar and outlines in the first place
best_for: Reading how prefix-allowed-tokens constraint enforcement works, in about 150 lines of Python you can fully understand
Beam search or batched generation with per-sequence different constraints, where the README's own table says the alternatives are weaker
Cases where you want the model to control JSON whitespace and field ordering rather than emitting canonical JSON
Keeping an existing vLLM deployment working with `--guided-decoding-backend lm-format-enforcer` during a migration
avoid_for: New projects - start with the current default structured-generation backend of your serving engine rather than choosing this library directly
Latency-sensitive per-token paths where a C++ implementation exists

Local LoRA or fine-tuned-model workflows where you want the model to own the format; the README's comparison table marks LoRA support as absent, and output-format training (e.g. Llama-3.x JSON fine-tunes) is usually the better answer
notes: The niche's clearest example of a project kept alive by being a documented fallback rather than a default. Kept as a record because the demotion is the useful fact: XGrammar (2024/11 SGLang, 2024/12 vLLM) took the default slot out from under it.
